summary: Targeted rules hardening and seven emulator checks passed. This assessment covers the changed source, not deployed production rules. Legacy sensitive data and remaining validation gaps prevent a secure certification.

findings.issue: Legacy inline payment proofs remain readable with their order documents; new proof documents are denied to direct clients and served through authorization checks.
findings.recommendation: Back up and migrate legacy proofs to private storage, remove inline proof fields, and test staff versus manager access before rollout.

findings.issue: Some admin-managed metadata collections retain broad validators and history queries lack pagination.
findings.recommendation: Add collection-specific field/type/size limits and bounded pagination while preserving valid existing schemas.

findings.issue: Legacy identity/scope fields and direct-write workflows may not satisfy the hardened rules. The local default-database emulator does not verify Enterprise named-database production behavior.
findings.recommendation: Validate existing records and all supported roles in staging; migrate legacy fields and implement outstanding backend workflows before enabling them.

findings.issue: Legacy client audit logs are not equivalent to the immutable server transaction audit and must not be trusted as authoritative financial history.
findings.recommendation: Use transaction_audit for financial evidence and migrate remaining important mutations to server-authored audit entries.
